name: problem
text: One in six people lives with a disability. To a screen reader, this online shop sounds like: image. Link. Image. Forty-seven accessibility failures. And in Europe, since June 2025, that's a legal problem.

captions.text: One in six people lives with a disability.

name: agent
text: Jangkau is an agent that doesn't just audit the page. It fixes it. Every edit is re-checked in a real browser, and if it breaks anything, it's rolled back and tried again.

captions.text: Jangkau is an agent that doesn't just audit the page.
Every edit is re-checked in a real browser,
it's rolled back and tried again.

name: neatlogs
text: We traced every run with neatlogs, then set up a detection that flags each rule the agent failed to fix. Here's what it caught.

captions.text: We traced every run with neatlogs,
then set up a detection that flags each rule the agent failed to fix.

name: incident1
text: Incident one. Our first verifier rejected correct label fixes. The span told us why: it counted rules still waiting in the queue as breakage. We fixed the check, and the shop went from forty-seven failures to zero.

captions.text: Our first verifier rejected correct label fixes.
it counted rules still waiting in the queue as breakage.
and the shop went from forty-seven failures to zero.

name: incident2
text: Incident two, on a real Bootstrap template. Contrast fixes kept failing. The traces showed a pixel diff punishing correct recolors, and then a hidden opacity of zero point six five. Edge-map diffs, measured feedback, and escalation to a stronger model took it from thirty-three to zero.

captions.text: The traces showed a pixel diff punishing correct recolors,
and then a hidden opacity of zero point six five.
and escalation to a stronger model took it from thirty-three to zero.

name: incident3
text: Incident three, on the W3C's own inaccessible demo page. The Execution Failed detection caught one bad edit throwing away nineteen good ones. Now valid edits are kept: sixty-seven failures down to four.

captions.text: on the W3C's own inaccessible demo page.

name: ci
text: It also runs in CI, as a GitHub Action. Every failure lands in code scanning, mapped to WCAG and to the European standard, EN 301 549.

text: Entire recorded the coding sessions behind these fixes, as checkpoints on our commits.

name: cfo
text: And cfo.ai modeled the business: about six cents per page, an eighty-three percent gross margin, and a downside case that set our fair-use rule.

text: Jangkau. So the web reaches everyone.
